title: CS 209: Java Basics
description: How Java runs, printing and concatenation, escape sequences, variables, types and division. Covers lectures 9-24 through 10-1.

cards.definition: Java Virtual Machine: runs bytecode and produces the output.
Java Runtime Environment: the JVM plus Java's built-in libraries. Everything needed to RUN Java.
Java Development Kit: the JRE plus the compiler (javac) and dev tools. Needed to WRITE and compile Java.
What javac turns your .java source into (.class files). Platform-independent; the JVM runs it.
Runs in 2 stages: source → bytecode (compile time), then bytecode → JVM (runtime). Java is one.
Runs in 1 stage, line by line. Python is one.
Caught going from source to bytecode: syntax errors (missing ;), type mismatch, undeclared variable. The program never runs.
Happens while the bytecode runs on the JVM: file does not exist, no permission, divide by zero.
Everything between a pair of curly braces. Every { needs a matching }.
The program's entry point. public = visible anywhere, static = no object needed, void = returns nothing, args = command-line arguments.
Return type meaning the method returns nothing; it only executes.
println prints then moves to a new line (ln = line). print stays on the same line.
If either side of + is a String, + joins text instead of adding. Evaluated left to right.
A backslash makes the next character mean something special (or normal): \" quote, \\ backslash, \n new line, \t tab.
A note in the code that Java ignores, like # in Python.
A named memory location that stores a value of a specific data type.
Declare: int price;  Initialize: price = 2;  Both at once: int price = 2;
Primitive whole number, 4 bytes. e.g. 1, 2, 3, 5
Primitive number with a fraction, 8 bytes. e.g. 2.3. Storing 2 gives 2.0
Primitive true/false. Default false for fields (local variables have no default).
Primitive single character in single quotes, 2 bytes. e.g. 'a'. Each char has a number code ('A' = 65).
An object type (not primitive): a sequence of characters in double quotes.
Returns the remainder of a division. 15 % 2 is 1.
int / int gives an int: the fraction is dropped. 5 / 2 is 2.
If either side is a double, the result is a double (Java picks the bigger type). 5.0 / 2 is 2.5
Input → Process → Output. The way to plan a program before writing it.
Can contain digits but cannot START with one. Convention: start lowercase (camelCase).

questions.explanation: Left to right: 1 + 2 = 3 (both numbers). Then 3 + "3" becomes text "33", and from there 4 and 5 are appended as text.
Two chars added together are numbers: 'a' (97) + 'b' (98) = 195. Only then does the String "c" show up and turn it into text.
The String is first this time, so each char is appended as a character. Same pieces as 'a' + 'b' + "c", opposite result.
* goes before +, so 5 * 2 = 10 first. Then "5" + 10 joins as text: 510.
Without the parentheses you get Sum: 34. a + b + "Sum: " gives 7Sum: . Anything inside quotes is printed literally.
Left to right: 7 / 2 is integer division = 3. Then 3 * 2.0 = 6.0, a double because 2.0 is a double.
x / 2 is int / int, so it is 3 BEFORE it is stored. Storing 3 in a double prints 3.0. The double type doesn't rescue the division.
% has the same precedence as * and /, so it happens before +. 3 % 2 = 1, then 10 + 1 = 11.
3 * 4 = 12, then 12 % 5 = 2 (same level, left to right), then 2 + 2 = 4.
9 / 2 = 4 (integer division) and 9 % 2 = 1, so 4 + 1 = 5.
A whole number fits in a double (it becomes 4.0). 4.0 can't go into an int, "x" is a String, not a char, and a boolean is only true or false.

questions.prompt: Which name is legal AND follows the naming convention for a variable?
questions.explanation: TotalScore compiles, but an uppercase start is the convention for class names. 2ndScore starts with a digit, and names can't contain spaces.

questions.prompt: A program has a typo on line 2 (printn instead of println), and line 5 divides by zero. What happens when you try to run it?
choices: It won't compile, so nothing prints
It prints line 1, then stops at the typo
It runs until the divide by zero, then crashes
It skips the typo and runs everything else
questions.answer: It won't compile, so nothing prints
questions.explanation: Compiling is stage 1. A compile error means no bytecode is produced, so stage 2 (running) never starts and the divide by zero is never reached.

questions.prompt: You send a friend only Welcome.class. What do they need to run it?
choices: A JRE (the JVM plus Java's libraries)
The JDK and the original Welcome.java
Nothing; .class files run on their own
questions.answer: A JRE (the JVM plus Java's libraries)
questions.explanation: .class is already bytecode, so compiling is done. Running bytecode needs a JVM and the standard libraries, which is the JRE.

questions.prompt: You compiled Welcome.java on Windows. Will that same Welcome.class run on a Mac?
choices: Yes, the Mac's JVM runs the same bytecode
No, it must be recompiled on the Mac
Only if the Mac also has javac
Only if you also send the .java file
questions.answer: Yes, the Mac's JVM runs the same bytecode
questions.explanation: Bytecode is platform-independent: write once, run anywhere. Each OS has its own JVM that understands the same bytecode.

questions.prompt: Which expression gives the seconds left over after the full minutes?
questions.explanation: % gives the remainder: 125 % 60 = 5. total / 60 is the minutes (2), and (total / 60) * 60 is the 120 seconds that ARE full minutes.

questions.prompt: Which line prints exactly:  She said "hi"
questions.explanation: A bare " ends the String early (compile error). Single quotes are only for one char. \h isn't a valid escape. Only \" puts a quote inside a String.

questions.prompt: How many lines of output does this produce?
questions.explanation: A, B, an empty line (the \n\n with nothing between them), then C.
The empty String "" is first, so 1 and 2 are each appended as text. This is a handy trick for joining numbers.
The numbers come first and add to 3. Only then is it joined to the empty String.
\n is a new line, so x and y go on separate lines.
\\ is ONE backslash. What's left after it is a plain n, so no new line happens: it prints a\nb.
3 * 4 = 12 happens first (precedence). Then left to right: "Total: " + 12 is text, and + 1 appends 1.
char + int does math on the char's number: 'B' is 66, so this is 67. No String is involved, so it stays a number.
Starting with "" makes everything after it text, so the char shows as B and the 1 is appended.
print doesn't end the line, so two joins one. println then ends that line, so three starts a new one.
3725 / 3600 = 1. Then s % 3600 = 125, and 125 / 60 = 2 (% and / go left to right). An IPO time converter in one line.
Read it in pairs: \" is a quote, \\ is a backslash, \" is a quote. So: quote, backslash, quote.
b is 2.0, so a / b = 2.0 (a double). a % 3 = 1. 2.0 + 1 = 3.0, still a double.
* happens before +, so 19.99 * 2 = 39.98 first, then it's joined to "$".

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of b?
questions.explanation: b = a copies the value 5 into b's own storage. Changing a afterwards doesn't touch b.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of avg?
questions.explanation: 256 / 3 is int / int = 85, and the .33 is lost BEFORE it reaches the double. This is the classic average-calculator bug. Fix it with score / 3.0.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of s?
questions.explanation: m becomes 3, then s is overwritten with 200 % 60 = 20. A variable holds only its latest value.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of count?
questions.explanation: The right side is worked out first using the OLD value (3 * 2 + 3 = 9), then stored back into count.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: 10 / 4 = 2 (integer division), stored as 2.0. Then 2.0 * 2 = 4.0. If you said 5.0, you divided before thinking about the types.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of c?
questions.explanation: 7 / 2 * 2 = 6, and 7 % 2 = 1, so 6 + 1 = 7. Quotient times divisor plus remainder always rebuilds the original number.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of code?
questions.explanation: 'a' is 97, so 97 + 2 = 99. It's stored in an int, so it stays a number, not 'c'.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Both parts use the old x (10): 10 % 4 = 2 and 10 / 4 = 2, so x becomes 4.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of s?
questions.explanation: s is a String, so + 1 + 1 appends text twice: A11, not A2.
age + gpa is a double (22.7). Storing a double in an int could lose data, so the compiler refuses.
Line 3 is missing its semicolon. That's a syntax error, caught at compile time.
Java is case-sensitive: the class is System with a capital S. The lowercase version doesn't exist.
b is declared on line 2 but never given a value. Declaring it is fine; USING it before it has a value is the error.
Single quotes hold exactly one char. A String needs double quotes.
"Score: " + score is already a String, and you can't subtract 5 from a String. Use parentheses: "Score: " + (score - 5).
A variable name can't start with a digit. firstPlace or place1 would work.

questions.prompt: This compiles. Which line crashes when it runs?
questions.explanation: Integer divide by zero isn't caught by the compiler. It crashes at runtime (ArithmeticException) after Start has already printed.
5.0 / 2 is 2.5, a double, which can't be stored in an int. Line 1 is fine: 5 is stored as 5.0.
X and x are different names in Java. X was never declared, so the compiler says "cannot find symbol".

questions.prompt: Which tool turns Welcome.java into Welcome.class?
choices: javac, the compiler (part of the JDK)
questions.answer: javac, the compiler (part of the JDK)
questions.explanation: javac does stage 1 (source → bytecode). The JVM only does stage 2: running the bytecode.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a RUNTIME error rather than a compile-time error?
choices: Dividing an int by a variable that holds 0
Using a variable that was never declared
questions.answer: Dividing an int by a variable that holds 0
questions.explanation: The compiler can't know what value a variable will hold, so int division by a zero variable only fails while running. The other three are caught before the program runs.

choices: So the JVM can call it without creating an object first
questions.answer: So the JVM can call it without creating an object first
questions.explanation: static means the method belongs to the class itself. Returning nothing is what void means.

questions.prompt: In main(String[] args), what is args?
choices: The command-line arguments, as an array of Strings
A list of the variables in main
questions.answer: The command-line arguments, as an array of Strings
questions.explanation: The parameters go inside the ( ). String[] means an array of Strings, which holds whatever was typed after the program name.
'7' is a char whose code is 55, not the number 7. char + int is math on the code: 55 + 1 = 56.
7 + 3 = 10 first (both numbers). The "" then turns everything after it into text: "10" + 7 + 3 gives 1073.
Left to right: 10 / 4 = 2 (integer division), then 2 * 4 = 8. Doing the * first would give 10, but / and * are evaluated left to right.
When the left number is smaller, it goes in 0 times, so the remainder is the whole left number: 3 % 7 = 3.
A whole number can go into a double; it's stored (and printed) as 4.0.
\U isn't a valid escape, so the single-backslash version won't compile. Writing \\ inside a String gives one backslash.
Everything after // on a line is a comment, so the second println never runs.

questions.prompt: How many lines of output does this produce?
questions.explanation: abc ends the first line (println), then d starts the second line and nothing ends it: "abc" and "d".
A boolean is exactly true or false, lowercase, no quotes. "false" is a String, 0 is an int, and False doesn't exist (Java is case-sensitive).
3 % 7 = 3 (7 doesn't fit into 3) and 7 % 3 = 1, so 3 + 1 = 4.
2 * 3 = 6 first. Then left to right: "A" + 6 is "A6", and + 4 appends 4.
Two chars added are numbers: 65 + 66 = 131. No String anywhere, so it stays a number.
\\ inside a String is one backslash. (\t would have been a tab: that's why the backslash has to be escaped.)
Each \" is a quote character inside its String, so the 5 ends up between two quotes.
Both parentheses are worked out first (3 and 7), then joined as text by the "".

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of b?
questions.explanation: After a = b, a is 2 and the old 1 is gone. So b = a puts 2 back into b. This is why swapping two variables needs a third, temporary one.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of d?
questions.explanation: 9 / 2 = 4 (integer division), then 4 + 0.5 = 4.5.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of s?
questions.explanation: Line 1: 1 + 2 = 3 first, giving "3x". Line 2: s is a String, so 1 and 2 are appended as text.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of n?
questions.explanation: Chars are numbers underneath: 'd' (100) - 'a' (97) = 3. This trick gives a letter's position in the alphabet, counting from 0.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of mins?
questions.explanation: 1000 / 60 = 16 full groups of 60 (960), so 1000 % 60 = 40 left over.

questions.prompt: After this runs, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: 5 / 2 = 2 (the .5 is dropped), then 2 * 2 = 4. Dividing then multiplying back doesn't undo integer division.
"true" in quotes is a String, not a boolean. It must be the bare word true.
Double quotes make a String. A char needs single quotes: 'A'.
x is already declared on line 1. To change it, write x = 2; without the type.
total is used without ever being declared. It needs a type: int total = price * 2;
5 is an int and can't be stored in a String variable. "5" (in quotes) would work.

questions.prompt: This compiles. Which line crashes when it runs?
questions.explanation: b is 3, so c is 3 - 3 = 0. a / c divides by zero, which only fails when the program runs.
The String on line 3 never closes, so the compiler reports an unclosed string literal.
The type is String with a capital S. Java is case-sensitive, so string isn't a type it knows.
